question: Can I work at a restaurant that serves pork or alcohol if I can't find any other job?
asked: I cannot find a job and I'm not able to pay for my livelihood. I'm forced by circumstance to work at a restaurant that serves haram. What is the verdict on this?
answer:
So the brother was unclear. He says "serves haram," so I'm going to give a generic response based upon this.

First and foremost, realize: our Prophet ﷺ said (hadith in Sahih Bukhari), "Whenever Allah makes something haram, He makes its price haram as well." This hadith is in Abu Dawud. Memorize this as a principle of Islam: if it is haram for you to use, it is haram for you to do what? To sell. If it's haram to use, it's haram to sell. If it's haram for you to eat or drink, it is haram to make financial benefit off of this.

And the hadith in Sahih Muslim: Jabir ibn Abdullah said that the Prophet ﷺ said (four things are mentioned): Allah has made it haram to buy and sell alcohol, and to buy and sell dead animals. Dead animals means an animal you find on the side of the road. The Arabs of Jahiliyyah, they didn't do dhabh. The Arabs of Jahiliyyah, if an animal died naturally, they would eat it, and this is maytah. It is disgusting. Allah says it is fisq; leave it. They would eat and they would sell the animal, maytah. Number three, al-khinzir; we all know khinzir. And number four, asnam, idols.

Now, the Prophet ﷺ is speaking to Muslims. No Muslim eats khinzir. What is the hadith saying? Allah has forbidden what? Bay', the buying and selling of khinzir, of idols.

I was really hurt when I went to Jerusalem to see our Muslim brothers selling icons of other faiths, icons of other faith traditions, amulets, salibs, like this. They're selling this. This is not allowed in our religion. It's not allowed to make money by selling idols. Let's say a person is living in a land where there are idols, and a Muslim says, "I'm not going to worship the idol, I'm just going to carve it and sell it." No, you cannot. And this is the worst selling out of all of this: to sell an idol.

Now, this is the hadith: somebody said, "Ya Rasulallah, can we sell the fat of the dead animal? At least let us sell the fat of the dead animal, because this fat, we use it on the ships, we put it on there to protect it from the water." What's the word in English? I forgot. Paraffin, or something you put on; sealant. It's a type of sealant. "So this fat, ya Rasulallah, can we sell this fat?" The Prophet ﷺ said, "Qatala Allahu al-Yahud," may Allah ʿazza wa jall curse this group of people. Why? Because, "inna Allaha lamma harrama shuhumaha": when Allah forbade them to utilize dead animals, they converted these animals into a type of salty solution, they decomposed it partially, they did whatever they wanted to, then they sold that najis, and then they benefited from that profit. Because of that, Allah's curse is on them. This hadith is in Sahih Muslim. So this is an explicit hadith that even if you do not benefit from the haram, you cannot sell the haram.

And we have the hadith in Sahih Muslim as well (all these are evidences that you should know and be aware of) that when Allah revealed that khamr is haram, the Prophet ﷺ sent the commandment: everybody pour your khamr into the streets. As you know, the famous incident: an Ansari came and said, "Ya Rasulallah, I am in charge of two orphans, and their father left a treasure of wine." Their father left many gallons, many caskets of wine. "And they are my" (whatever, nephews, or whatever you want to call them; these are distant relatives) "but they're orphans. This is their money. This is their rizq. This is a fortune for them. They're orphans. Can I sell..." Now, who would he sell this to? Muslims? No. Medina is a multicultural society. "Can I sell these caskets and then give them the money?"

Now, before I answer (and you all know the answer, by the way), why is this hadith so important? Can anybody tell me? Orphans. The money of orphans is the highest category of sanctity. Anybody who devours the property of orphans with zulm, Allah is saying, you are eating the fire of Hell into your belly. A'udhu billah. The highest level of sanctity in the Shari'ah when it comes to money is the money of orphans. You are not allowed to touch it unless you have to, because you are dying or starving; you have to get a little bit to feed the kids. Otherwise it must remain untouched until the orphans come of age. You all know this, right? If there were to be any exception, it would be for the orphans.

So our Prophet ﷺ said, "No, spill all of it out," and he did not allow an exception. And subhanAllah, also, this money was halal one day ago, before the prohibition. So if there would have been an exception, somebody could have said, "Okay, you know what, the Shari'ah just came down, the father died in Jahiliyyah, the young kids are now Muslim, they're orphans." If there could have been an exception, it would have been for them. But what did our Prophet ﷺ say? "No, get rid of it." Whenever Allah has forbidden something, He has forbidden its buying and selling.

So, based upon all of this, we say: **the default is that it is haram to buy and sell that which is haram for you to consume.**

Now, that having been said, as we said many times, there are levels of haram. Selling an idol is definitely the worst thing we can possibly sell; there's nothing worse than selling an idol. Selling sharab is something Allah has cursed; it is something that Allah's la'nah is upon. Selling khinzir is something that our Prophet ﷺ explicitly forbade; Allah has forbidden the selling of khinzir. But they're not at the same level. Idolatry is much higher, khinzir is definitely bad, and sharab is middle; it's like a la'nah.

For example, selling non-zabiha meat would not come under this hadith, because non-zabiha meat that has been slaughtered, we said, this is a controversy between the Shafi'is and the Hanafis. So if somebody is working in a restaurant that has non-zabiha meat, in this case, inshallah, that tahrim does not apply. Because even if you don't eat (as I said, I personally would not eat that meat), in this case the Shafi'i madhhab allows it and considers it to be halal.

Now, that having been said, AMJA, the American Muslim Jurist Association, has released a very detailed fatwa about this issue, and they've basically taken into account that sometimes a person does not have an alternative, and it might be a type of darurah. So AMJA has given a fatwa, and I'm reading the fatwa directly from them: "It is not permissible for a Muslim to work at any grocery store or restaurant where prohibited items are sold if this work would entail direct involvement with serving alcohol or pork products." So this is the generic. Then they said: "However, cases of exigent need" (means darurah, dire need) "should be taken into account. Each one is judged in accordance with its personal extent."

Now somebody comes and says, "I don't have any job, I cannot pay rent, I'm going to sleep on the streets, and the only job I'm getting is at a Subway," let's say, "and I'm working 40 hours a week at the Subway, and sometimes I have to use the pork over there." So we say this is a darurah. And the fatwa says: if that type of darurah is there, then in your heart you don't like what you are doing, and you actively seek alternative employment. You don't just become comfortable; you actively seek an alternative. But for that duration, if you're going to get kicked onto the streets, this is a type of darurah.

So we say: the one who wants to earn supplemental income, the teenager who's living at home and he's looking for a secondary job just to get some... What are the games? Wii? Or is Wii outdated? I don't know. PS4? I don't know, whatever it is. What is it? PS4 is outdated too? What is the latest game? Xbox 3 or 10? I don't know what it is. So whatever. So the teenager: you want to put some stability on him, say, "Go get a job." Excellent, he should get a job. But he doesn't need the money to pay rent. So this person, you cannot allow him to get a job where he has to fry pork products. This is supplemental income; the standard is going to be higher. You understand?

Now, a person has come from a foreign land, and at that stage they are sending résumés everywhere, their resources are dwindling, and at that stage, generally speaking, most of the work is going to be a type of manual labor that might have a little bit of haram. We say: choose the least amount of haram. So for example, a restaurant that serves lots of non-zabiha meat and a little bit of pork is infinitely better than a restaurant that serves sharab, right? So you will choose the one that has... Because selling pork is haram; selling alcohol is la'nah. There's a much worse level than this.

So we say, as the maxim of fiqh goes, that every exceptional situation we look at in terms of its exceptional situation: how difficult it is, the more laxity. There's a principle in the Shari'ah: the more difficult the situation, the easier the Shari'ah is. The more difficult the situation, the easier the Shari'ah becomes, and the easier the person's situation is, the more strict the Shari'ah will become.

And therefore, to conclude this point, we say: **the person who is forced by circumstance to work in haram, and there's no alternative, should find the least haram level**, because there are levels of haram. And if he is forced, his heart must hate it, and he must actively search for employment.
